sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即便是在我还在夜店打碟的黑胶唱片时代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 每晚你都要带着你最珍视的 300 件宝贝去工作，把 DJ 台变成一个充满 50 年历史精美文物的流动博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》。

sentences.en: Hey, it's Michael.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是迈克尔。

sentences.en: For the last few months here on The Daily, we've been bringing you The Run-Up, our show about the midterm elections and how we got to this fraught moment in American politics.
sentences.zh: 过去几个月里，我们一直在《每日新闻》节目中为您带来《冲刺》，这是我们关于中期选举以及我们是如何走到美国政治这一紧要关头的节目。

sentences.en: Today, in the final episode of the season, we look at the results and what they tell us about where we might be headed next.
sentences.zh: 今天，在本季的最后一集中，我们将审视选举结果，看看它们揭示了我们未来可能走向何方。

sentences.en: Take a listen.
sentences.zh: 请听。

sentences.en: The state of democracy right now is very shaky.
sentences.zh: 目前的民主状况非常动摇。

sentences.en: From the beginning, these midterms were about democracy.
sentences.zh: 从一开始，这次中期选举就与民主息息相关。

sentences.en: I'm worried that democracy is being eroded.
sentences.zh: 我担心民主正在受到侵蚀。

sentences.en: Our democratic system is under direct threat.
sentences.zh: 我们的民主制度正受到直接威胁。

sentences.en: I think democracy, I think it's much more fragile than I realize.
sentences.zh: 我认为民主，我觉得它比我意识到的要脆弱得多。

sentences.en: But as I stand here tonight, equality and democracy are under assault.
sentences.zh: 但今晚我站在这里，平等和民主正受到攻击。

sentences.en: When President Biden made that, his central message to voters.
sentences.zh: 当拜登总统将其作为他向选民传达的核心信息时。

sentences.en: I'm asking our nation to come together, unite behind the single purpose of defending our democracy regardless of your ideology.
sentences.zh: 我请求我们的国家团结起来，为了捍卫我们民主这一单一目标而联合，无论你的意识形态如何。

sentences.en: The question was not whether Americans believe democracy was on the ballot.
sentences.zh: 问题不在于美国人是否相信民主在选票上。

sentences.en: It was how strong their commitment to democracy really was.
sentences.zh: 而在于他们对民主的承诺到底有多坚定。

sentences.en: And that's where I want to address something that's bugging me for a long time.
sentences.zh: 这就是我想谈谈困扰我很久的一件事的地方。

sentences.en: Would voters care?
sentences.zh: 选民会在意吗？

sentences.en: We are a constitutional republic.
sentences.zh: 我们是一个宪政共和国。

sentences.en: We are not a democracy.
sentences.zh: 我们不是一个民主国家。

sentences.en: Nor in the Constitution does it use the word democracy.
sentences.zh: 宪法中甚至没有使用“民主”这个词。

sentences.en: Would they reject a growing anti-democratic sentiment taking hold at the state level?
sentences.zh: 他们会拒绝在州一级蔓延的反民主情绪吗？

sentences.en: As our president says, we worship God, not government.
sentences.zh: 正如我们的总统所说，我们崇拜上帝，而不是政府。

sentences.en: God bless you.
sentences.zh: 上帝保佑你们。

sentences.en: A hardened strain of Christianity gaining ground across the Republican base.
sentences.zh: 一种强硬的基督教派别正在共和党基层获得支持。

sentences.en: We do not consent to knee-camping our governor before he even takes office.
sentences.zh: 我们不同意在州长上任前就对他进行跪拜。

sentences.en: We do not consent to you silencing our votes.
sentences.zh: 我们不同意你们压制我们的投票。

sentences.en: All of it enabled by elected officials who have been working to seize control of the structures of power.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是由那些致力于夺取权力结构的民选官员所促成的。

sentences.en: And when I asked Democratic lawmakers how they plan to combat all this.
sentences.zh: 当我问民主党议员他们打算如何应对这一切时。

sentences.en: Everybody who's listening to this podcast who cares about these issues needs to fight harder.
sentences.zh: 每一个关心这些问题的播客听众都需要更努力地抗争。

sentences.en: I mean, make phone calls.
sentences.zh: 我是说，去打电话。

sentences.en: Go door to door.
sentences.zh: 去挨家挨户走访。

sentences.en: They said people would have to vote harder and keep the faith.
sentences.zh: 他们说人们必须更积极地投票并保持信念。

sentences.en: America is not great because it is more enlightened than any other nation.
sentences.zh: 美国之所以伟大，并非因为它比任何其他国家都更开明。

sentences.en: But rather because it has always been able to repair its faults.
sentences.zh: 而是因为它总能修复自身的错误。

sentences.en: But it wasn't clear from polling whether that message was really gaining any traction.
sentences.zh: 但从民调中并不清楚这一信息是否真的产生了影响。

sentences.en: And so as members of his own party, brace for defeat.
sentences.zh: 因此，当他所在政党的成员准备迎接失败时。

sentences.en: In our bones, we know democracy is at risk.
sentences.zh: 我们从骨子里知道民主正处于危险之中。

sentences.en: But we also know this.
sentences.zh: 但我们也知道这一点。

sentences.en: It's within our power, each and every one of us, to preserve our democracy.
sentences.zh: 我们每个人都有能力捍卫我们的民主。

sentences.en: President Biden made one final plea.
sentences.zh: 拜登总统发出了最后一次呼吁。

sentences.en: You have the power.
sentences.zh: 你有力量。

sentences.en: It's your choice.
sentences.zh: 这是你的选择。

sentences.en: It's your decision.
sentences.zh: 这是你的决定。

sentences.en: The fate of the nation, the fate of the soul of America.
sentences.zh: 国家的命运，美国灵魂的命运。

sentences.en: Lies what it always does.
sentences.zh: 一如既往地。

sentences.en: With the people.
sentences.zh: 掌握在人民手中。

sentences.en: Turns out.
sentences.zh: 事实证明。

sentences.en: In your hands, in your heart, in your ballot.
sentences.zh: 掌握在你的手中，在你的心中，在你的选票里。

sentences.en: It kind of worked.
sentences.zh: 这确实起了一定作用。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Astead Herndon.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的阿斯特德·赫恩登。

sentences.en: This is the run-up.
sentences.zh: 这是《冲刺》节目。

sentences.en: Shane, have you recovered from last week?
sentences.zh: 肖恩，你从上周的忙碌中恢复过来了吗？

sentences.en: I mean, it's like one week ago for the formal end of the 2022 campaign.
sentences.zh: 我是说，距离 2022 年竞选正式结束才过去一周。

sentences.en: We haven't even called the House at this exact moment.
sentences.zh: 此时此刻我们甚至还没宣布众议院的最终结果。

sentences.en: And yet, we're about to have a 2024 campaign.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们马上又要迎来 2024 年的竞选了。

sentences.en: So I would say no.
sentences.zh: 所以我得说没有。

sentences.en: I have not.
sentences.zh: 我还没有。

sentences.en: I have not yet recovered.
sentences.zh: 我还没有恢复过来。

sentences.en: You know, I remember...
sentences.zh: 你知道，我记得……

sentences.en: Earlier this week, as the results from the midterms were still being processed.
sentences.zh: 本周早些时候，当中期选举的结果还在统计时。

sentences.en: I called my colleague, Shane Goldmacher.
sentences.zh: 我给我的同事肖恩·戈德马赫打了电话。

sentences.en: Shane, I'm really excited to have you on and to be able to do this.
sentences.zh: 肖恩，我很高兴你能来，也很高兴能做这期节目。

sentences.en: And for maybe the unaware, you're a national political correspondent, which means that pretty much your job is to understand the parties and where they're at, what they're up to,
sentences.zh: 对于可能不太了解的人，你是全国政治记者，这意味着你的工作基本上就是了解各党派的立场和动向，

sentences.en: what their message is, particularly at a high level.
sentences.zh: 了解他们的高层传达的信息。

sentences.en: In that context, I want to think about the midterms that we all just experienced.
sentences.zh: 在此背景下，我想回顾一下我们刚刚经历的中期选举。

sentences.en: How was the Democratic Party thinking about Joe Biden's message heading into the midterms?
sentences.zh: 民主党在进入中期选举时是如何看待乔·拜登的信息的？

sentences.en: And how was the party specifically thinking about his ask of voters to protect democracy over everything else?
sentences.zh: 该党又是如何具体看待他要求选民将捍卫民主置于一切之上的诉求的？

sentences.en: I mean, I would say the weekend before the midterms, the party was largely freaking out.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想说在中期选举前的那个周末，该党基本上处于恐慌状态。

sentences.en: They were freaking out about what they expected to be significant losses in the House of Representatives.
sentences.zh: 他们对众议院可能出现的重大失利感到恐慌。

sentences.en: They were freaking out about the possibility of also losing the Senate.
sentences.zh: 他们对可能失去参议院控制权也感到恐慌。

sentences.en: And when it came to the president, they were worried that he wasn't talking about the issue that in poll after poll was shown to be the top issue for voters in 2022,
sentences.zh: 而谈到总统时，他们担心他没有谈论民调中一再显示为 2022 年选民最关心的问题，

sentences.en: which was the economy and inflation.
sentences.zh: 也就是经济和通货膨胀。

sentences.en: And there was actually a moment just before the midterms that I think really captured this, which was Hillary Rosen, who is this longtime Democratic strategist,
sentences.zh: 事实上，在中期选举前有一个时刻我认为真正捕捉到了这一点，那就是希拉里·罗森，她是民主党的一位资深战略家，

sentences.en: been around forever, and she did the Sunday shows and she was on CNN.
sentences.zh: 她在这个圈子里待了很久，她上了周日节目，也上了 CNN。

sentences.en: And she sort of ripped into the Democrats and said, we have missed the message on this election.
sentences.zh: 她严厉批评了民主党人，说我们错过了这次选举的核心信息。

sentences.en: The voters keep telling us over and over, we care most about the economy.
sentences.zh: 选民们一遍又一遍地告诉我们，他们最关心的是经济。

sentences.en: And all we are doing is talking about how democracy is at stake.
sentences.zh: 而我们所做的只是在谈论民主正处于危险之中。

sentences.en: And we're sort of, this is the catchphrase in politics is like, meet people where they're at, right?
sentences.zh: 我们有点，这是政治中的流行语，就是“深入群众”，对吧？

sentences.en: So we were not meeting people where we're at.
sentences.zh: 所以我们并没有深入群众。

sentences.en: That was the concern that Democrats had over and over and over again, heading into the election.
sentences.zh: 这就是民主党人在选举前一遍又一遍担心的事。

sentences.en: I mean, one of the nights that I was working, one of the many nights that I was working late this last few weeks and I was in the office,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，过去几周我加班的那些夜晚里，有天晚上我还在办公室，

sentences.en: I stayed to cover Joe Biden's speech about democracy.
sentences.zh: 我留下来报道乔·拜登关于民主的演讲。

sentences.en: And I was in the office late enough to say,
sentences.zh: 我待在办公室很晚，以至于我说，

sentences.en: I'm taking a taxi home.
sentences.zh: 我要打车回家了。

sentences.en: And I remember calling, I talked to several Democrats on my taxi ride home.
sentences.zh: 我记得在回家的出租车上，我给几位民主党人打了电话。

sentences.en: And I was saying, hey, what did you think of the president's speech?
sentences.zh: 我说，嘿，你们觉得总统的演讲怎么样？

sentences.en: And they said, look, this is, I mean, it's fine.
sentences.zh: 他们说，听着，这，我是说，还行吧。

sentences.en: You know, they weren't against him giving a speech about democracy the week before the election, but it wasn't what their campaigns were about.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们并不反对他在选举前一周发表关于民主的演讲，但这并不是他们竞选的核心内容。

sentences.en: They felt that it was him talking about an important moral cause, but not necessarily something that was helpful politically.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得这是他在谈论一个重要的道德事业，但不一定对政治有帮助。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There was a feeling that Biden and other Democrats were overly focused on trying to convince voters to reject growing extremism.
sentences.zh: 有一种感觉是，拜登和其他民主党人过于专注于试图说服选民拒绝日益增长的极端主义。

sentences.en: And that maybe that wasn't something that the majority of Americans were all that troubled by.
sentences.zh: 也许这并不是大多数美国人所困扰的问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, there was a ton of criticism for Democrats for intervening a handful of these primaries to push these more extreme Republican candidates
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，民主党人因为干预了少数几场初选以推动那些更极端的共和党候选人而受到了大量批评，

sentences.en: who were successful in a house race in Michigan, where the Democrats backed a more extreme Republican who ousted in a primary, one of the 10 Republicans
sentences.zh: 这些候选人在密歇根州的一场众议院竞选中成功了，民主党人支持了一位更极端的共和党人，在初选中挤掉了那 10 位共和党人之一，

sentences.en: who had voted to impeach Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 那些曾投票弹劾唐纳德·特朗普的共和党人。

sentences.en: There was pushback to that.
sentences.zh: 对此有强烈的反对意见。

sentences.en: There was pushback to Democrats pushing through candidates, for instance, in Illinois for governor.
sentences.zh: 对于民主党人在伊利诺伊州州长竞选中推动候选人的做法也有反对意见。

sentences.en: And how the Democrats got a lot of, you know, can you say shit?
sentences.zh: 而民主党人因为这样做遇到了很多，你知道，可以说“烂摊子”吗？

sentences.en: While the Democrats got a lot of problems for doing that, you can lose fact that they were, there's a supply and demand issue here, which is the Republican electorate
sentences.zh: 虽然民主党人因为这样做遇到了很多麻烦，但你不能忽视一个事实，那就是这里存在供需问题，即共和党选民，

sentences.en: you know, there was demand for these kinds of candidates.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对这类候选人是有需求的。

sentences.en: So the Democrats helped supply the candidates, but the voters were looking for them.
sentences.zh: 所以民主党人帮助提供了这些候选人，但选民们确实在寻找他们。

sentences.en: And so when Joe Biden was talking about this, he was talking about a real phenomenon that the Republican Party was moving in this direction, that if you took the totality
sentences.zh: 所以当乔·拜登谈论这个问题时，他谈论的是一个真实的现象，即共和党正在向这个方向发展，如果你把 2022 年初选的全部情况加起来，

sentences.en: of the 2022 primaries,
sentences.zh: 2022 年的初选，

sentences.en: Donald Trump, for the most part, was winning in terms of getting candidates aligned with him through the Republican primaries.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普在很大程度上是赢家，因为他通过共和党初选让候选人与他保持一致。

sentences.en: And so when you look at how the results came out, his focus on democracy was part of a broader message that he was pushing.
sentences.zh: 所以当你审视选举结果时，他对比民主的关注是他所推动的更广泛信息的一部分。

sentences.en: It was part of a broader message that Democrats were pushing, which was this is a Republican Party that is so extreme that they will take away your democracy.
sentences.zh: 这是民主党人所推动的更广泛信息的一部分，即这是一个极端到会夺走你们民主的共和党。

sentences.en: They will take away your abortion rights.
sentences.zh: 他们会夺走你们的堕胎权。

sentences.en: They'll take away your social security.
sentences.zh: 他们会夺走你们的社会保障。

sentences.en: They'll take away your X, Y, and Z
sentences.zh: 他们会夺走你们的 X、Y 和 Z，

sentences.en: and put it all together.
sentences.zh: 把这一切加在一起。

sentences.en: And it seems like it had some success.
sentences.zh: 看起来这确实取得了一些成功。

sentences.en: Two things there.
sentences.zh: 这里有两点。

sentences.en: One, to highlight what you said, like, I think that is a core point.
sentences.zh: 第一，强调你所说的，我认为这是一个核心点。

sentences.en: You know, what we often talk about as bad candidates was really a reflection of what Republican voters wanted.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们经常谈论的“糟糕候选人”实际上反映了共和党选民想要什么。

sentences.en: The slate that Republicans had in this midterm, you know, as we've talked about on this show, was often driven by Republican voters who have wanted those grievances
sentences.zh: 正如我们在节目中讨论的那样，共和党在中期选举中的候选人名单，往往是由那些希望在候选人身上反映出这些不满的共和党选民所驱动的。

sentences.en: reflected in their candidates.
sentences.zh: 反映在他们的候选人身上。

sentences.en: But then the second thing here is like, I mean, it wasn't fully out of left field for people to question that democracy messaging strategy, right?
sentences.zh: 但第二点是，我是说，人们质疑那种民主信息策略并非完全不可理喻，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, to your point, polling did consistently show that Americans ranked economy as the top concern, concerns about inflation as a broader concern.
sentences.zh: 就像你说的，民调确实一致显示美国人将经济列为首要关注点，对通货膨胀的担忧是更广泛的担忧。

sentences.en: How should we think about that type of issue-based polling that told us that consistently throughout the year and what we know to be true now,
sentences.zh: 我们应该如何看待那种全年都一致告诉我们这一点的基于议题的民调，以及我们现在所知道的事实，

sentences.en: which is that voters were really concerned about democracy and protecting the political system?
sentences.zh: 即选民确实非常关心民主和保护政治制度？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I think the real question is about how do you ask people what are the issues you care most about?
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，我认为真正的问题在于你如何询问人们他们最关心的问题是什么？

sentences.en: Because in poll after poll, including the New York Times poll that we did in October, overwhelmingly, inflation and the economy were the top issues.
sentences.zh: 因为在一次又一次的民调中，包括我们在十月份做的《纽约时报》民调，通货膨胀和经济压倒性地成为了首要议题。

sentences.en: It was 44% of voters said those were the top issues for them.
sentences.zh: 有 44% 的选民表示这些是他们最关心的问题。

sentences.en: And democracy, you know, that was down at the 8%, 9% range.
sentences.zh: 而民主，你知道，那是在 8% 到 9% 的范围内。

sentences.en: And so if you're going to say, well, what's the most important issue?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你要问，什么是最重要的问题？

sentences.en: You know, I think the issue, the most important issue of the 2022 elections was probably the economy and inflation, but it doesn't mean that it was the decisive issue.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为 2022 年选举最重要的问题可能是经济和通货膨胀，但这并不意味着它是决定性的问题。

sentences.en: And I think that that's, that's where you got into what the democratic messaging was, which was it was trying to take this election and for voters say, look,
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是民主党信息策略的切入点，即它试图抓住这次选举，对选民说，看，

sentences.en: you might not like the economy.
sentences.zh: 你可能不喜欢经济状况。

sentences.en: You might not like Joe Biden, but if you go to the voting booth, don't just think about the economy.
sentences.zh: 你可能不喜欢乔·拜登，但如果你去投票站，不要只考虑经济。

sentences.en: Don't just think about Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 不要只考虑乔·拜登。

sentences.en: Think about the broader consequences for this country.
sentences.zh: 考虑一下这对这个国家更广泛的后果。

sentences.en: Don't make it a referendum on Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 不要把它变成对乔·拜登的公投。

sentences.en: Don't say, I don't like Joe Biden, so we're going to vote for the Republicans.
sentences.zh: 不要说，我不喜欢乔·拜登，所以我们要投票给共和党人。

sentences.en: Say, I don't like Joe Biden, but I also really do value abortion rights.
sentences.zh: 要说，我不喜欢乔·拜登，但我确实非常重视堕胎权。

sentences.en: But I also really do value
